summary.headline: Avanti Feeds Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT fell 12.8% YoY to INR 184 crore as feed raw-material costs spiked; FY26 PBT rose 20% to INR 882 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated gross income rose 5.9% YoY to INR 1,515 crore in Q4 FY26, but PBT declined 12.8% YoY to INR 184 crore and 17.1% QoQ, mainly from the feed division. Feed division PBT fell 28% YoY to INR 139 crore on higher fish meal and soya bean meal costs and lower Q4 volume. Shrimp processing and export PBT rose to INR 48 crore from INR 18 crore a year earlier on better realisations, FX and lower ocean freight. Management flagged a sharp raw-material price spike in the last two months and said a feed price hike is being finalised.

segments.name: Feed division
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 feed sales were 1,23,725 MT (vs 1,18,127 MT in Q3, 1,29,711 MT in Q4 FY25); FY26 volume 5,62,060 MT vs 5,55,248 MT. PBT margin in FY26 was about 15.5% of revenue vs 14.34% in FY25.

segments.name: Shrimp processing and export
segments.commentary: FY26 gross income INR 1,741 crore (+43%) on volume up 2,827 MT (about 20%) and better realisations; Q4 PBT of INR 48 crore absorbed a one-off gratuity and leave encashment provision under the new labour code.

segments.name: Pet care (Avant Furst)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales were INR 151 lakh vs INR 136 lakh in Q3. Volume rose from 53 tonnes to about 100 tonnes, with a target of 800 MT by year-end; 31 distributors across 13 cities. Products are imported from Thailand until own plant is ready.

guidance_outlook: Feed sales FY27 estimated at about 5,80,000 MT vs 5,62,060 MT in FY26, against an estimated calendar 2026 shrimp output of 8-9 lakh MT and feed consumption of 11-12 lakh MT.
Shrimp exports FY27 estimated at about 19,000 MT vs 16,976 MT in FY26 (the call also referenced FY25 in this context, which appears to be a transcription slip).
Management targets 10-15% overall growth over the next two to three years, described as a big achievement given uncertainty.
No major capex foreseen over the next two years; Hyderabad pet food plant awaits DPR and government approvals before construction.
Feed price increase to be announced within about 10 days of the call, to offset steep raw-material cost increases.
capex_capacity: Shrimp processing capacity is about 26,000-28,000 MT on paper, but the business is seasonal and utilisation is constrained by raw-material availability.
Management said it is not planning major capex in the next two years, but will raise capacity utilisation and add value-added products.
Pet food: land near Hyderabad converted to non-agricultural use; land development in progress, final designs and DPR under preparation, construction to start after government approvals.
Ecuador investment made in partnership with a local party (per management).
demand_pricing: Fish meal consumption price rose to INR 130/kg in Q4 FY26 from INR 117 in Q3 and INR 91 a year earlier; purchase price now INR 230/kg. Management said fish meal doubled from INR 100 to INR 240 over May and June.
Soya bean meal rose to INR 55/kg in Q4 FY26 from INR 44 in Q3 and INR 41 a year earlier; current purchase price INR 72/kg. Wheat flour eased to INR 31/kg from INR 32 in Q3.
A feed price increase was taken in February 2026 but had only one month of impact; a further increase is planned.
Frozen shrimp exports in FY25-26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA imports fell 17.9% in volume, while China rose 24% and EU 36%.
Company shrimp exports rose to 16,976 MT in FY26 from 14,149 MT in FY25.
Management said about 75% of India's fish meal output is exported, driven by price and government incentives; it is lobbying for export limits and to allow soya bean meal imports.

qa_highlights.question: Why does FY27 feed offtake of 11-12 lakh MT imply flat demand, and how will the feed division perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a price increase is being worked out against market acceptance, with a specific figure expected in about 10 days; farm economics are described as good and the second quarter is key.

qa_highlights.question: What is the quantum of the Q4 price hike and how will feed margins move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the February price increase had limited Q4 impact, and another increase is planned to offset the steep fish meal and soya bean meal rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 export target of about 19,000 MT conservative versus peers and FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Executive director Nikhilesh said growth must be step by step given the business's build-up needs, citing quality and food-safety requirements for EU access.

qa_highlights.question: Is any major capex planned over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no big capex is foreseen in the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and cash burn of the pet care business?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume has risen from 53 to about 100 tonnes, with 31 distributors in 13 cities; own manufacturing is needed before cost benefits show, so the current focus is brand building.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US IEEPA tariff refund size and who is the importer of record?
qa_highlights.answer: Avanti Frozen Foods is the importer of record; refund claims are estimated at about USD 15-20 million, with processing expected to take time as anti-dumping reviews complete over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capacity headroom and why not expand faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is about 26,000-28,000 MT, but seasonal raw-material availability limits utilisation; management is focused on raising utilisation rather than adding capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the value-added shrimp mix changing, and will processing EBITDA margins rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added products (ready-to-eat, breaded, Japanese preparations) are a larger share than 10 years ago and yield margins above the market average, though they reduce factory output.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and profit growth is expected over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 10-15% overall growth, but said it cannot yet give a firm FY27 budget due to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned versus Ecuador, the largest exporter?
qa_highlights.answer: India is the number two exporter; management is positive on the US and Europe markets after the tariff changes.

risks_watch: Feed margin compression: fish meal and soya bean meal prices are rising steeply and the size and acceptance of the planned feed price hike are unknown.
Government policy on fish meal export limits, incentives and soya bean meal imports could change input costs.
US tariff refund (about USD 15-20 million) timing depends on anti-dumping reviews expected to take 12-18 months.
Shrimp output for FY27 depends on El Nino weather and the July-September crop season.
FY27 budgeting is not finalised, so guidance is indicative only.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and exports, but cautious and somewhat evasive on feed margins and FY27 budgets, citing raw-material volatility and uncertainty.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, when things were going smoothly, the prices of raw materials used for the manufacture of shrimp feed are going up steeply since past two months.
We don't foresee any big CapEx in the next two years.
Roughly, it will come around USD 15-20 million.
Overall, the target, if you put around 10-15% growth with the present global situation, it will be a big achievement.

adds.what: Hyderabad pet food plant (awaiting DPR and government approvals; no major capex planned in next two years)

growth.why: Management targets 10-15% growth over 2-3 years and estimates FY27 feed sales of ~5.8 lakh MT (vs 5.62 lakh MT in FY26) plus ~19,000 MT shrimp exports, with a feed price hike to offset raw-material costs; backing is partial (volume estimates and a pricing action, but no firm capacity additions and no major capex planned).
